title: Transfer: energy and work
target: Choose and justify energy methods in new physical situations.
criteria: Choose the correct energy terms and units.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A spring launches a cart up a ramp. Which ideal energy account includes the needed storage terms?
options: Only the final height without any initial energy.
Spring potential, gravitational potential, and kinetic energy.
cpa.guide: The relevant stores change between spring compression, motion, and elevation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A student combines 400 J with 0.6 kJ and reports 400.6 J. What is the corrected sum?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 1.5 kg object descends 3 m from rest with g = 10 N/kg. Resistance transfers 9 J out of mechanical energy. What is final K?
cpa.guide: Gravitational loss is 45 J; subtract 9 J to get 36 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A lift delivers 240 J in 12 s. What is average useful power?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A model predicts an impact’s energy accurately. What additional information is needed to predict detailed damage?
options: No additional information is ever needed.
Material response, contact geometry, and energy-transfer details.
Only a change from joules to watts.
cpa.guide: Energy constrains possibilities but does not uniquely determine damage.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Two routes have the same drop, but one includes resistance and the other is ideal. Which comparison is defensible for identical starts?
options: Both must have identical kinetic energy under all conditions.
Resistance creates additional kinetic energy automatically.
The ideal route violates total energy conservation.
The resisted route can end with less kinetic energy because some energy changes form.
cpa.guide: Include resistive transfers when applying an energy model to a new situation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
